title: Curve Mirror
description: A roadside convex mirror on an orange pole, standing over an old house at a level crossing in Kyoto. Drag to turn it on its bracket and the glass sweeps everything the photograph never showed: the street behind you, the road below, the sky over your head, and, turned far enough, the house and the crossing you are looking at, seen from where the mirror stands. At one angle it catches the sun.
intent: The Japanese curve mirror (カーブミラー, https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/カーブミラー), the convex road mirror at every blind corner, composited into a real photograph as a physical object, and reflecting correctly. Reality pieces research (factory/reality/techniques.md, idea 7, Curve mirror). The photograph is measured: MoGe-2 metric point map, the true vertical from the poles' vanishing point, the sun from the house's shading. The mirror is a traced sphere cap (800 mm, 1.6 m radius of curvature) reflecting one panorama centred on it: the photo's own pixels re-projected from the mirror's position in front of the lens, a CC0 360 of a Japanese residential street, given the photo's summer sky, behind it. Frame (a deep band with a visor over the top), shell, bracket and pole are lit by that panorama and the sun, cast their shadow on the house through the point map, and the glass is an acrylic dome standing proud of the frame, with a Fresnel sheen that climbs to its rim, the zenith's gloss on its upper bulge, the visor reflected at its crown, and dust and a smudge that scatter the sun. The plate's own enamels are graded down so the mirror is the one warm note against the cobalt (grade.py: where each is; the shader: how much of a pixel is, by a feathered hue window): the crossbuck's yellow to about two thirds of its chroma, turned toward a sun-faded ochre and a third of a stop down, the barrier pole's orange-red to two thirds, the green sign to half, in the plate and in the glass alike. Shot through a Black Pro-Mist (the top 15% of the frame's light, glass and plate alone, spread wide and screened back) and developed through the lab's summer film, its red layer halating a thin warm ring round the clouds. The drag turns it only as far as a real bracket does, 65 degrees either way and 35 down to 15 up, against sprung end-stops that stiffen past 55 and push it back off when let go, so its back is never turned to the lens; its weathered enamel is a rough dielectric (roughness about 0.6, the panorama prefiltered to that width for its sheen, no sun lobe), rolled off under white on the plate's shoulder so the sunlit side stays orange. ?aim=yaw,pitch holds the aim (degrees, held within that range), ?aim=sun holds the sun in the glass.

sources.author: PJH (@dokae)
sources.note: Ukyo, Kyoto (Ricoh GR II): a low-angle fumikiri crossbuck and lamps over an old tiled house. Resampled to 2464x1632 (photo.webp). Point map, normals and field of view: MoGe-2 ViT-S normal (Microsoft, MIT, https://huggingface.co/Ruicheng/moge-2-vits-normal-onnx) via tools/depth/normals.py; sky matte tools/depth/segment.py sky; its sky graded through that matte to a deep summer cobalt by elevation, deepening toward the zenith, clouds kept pale (sky_grade.py); its enamels graded down (grade.py). Baked by tools/depth/bakes/curve-mirror (vp.py vertical, bake.py panorama, distances, SH9, shadow aux).

sources.author: AsPJT (Wikimedia Commons)
sources.note: 端陵神社・端陵古墳（南）, March 2025: a 360 at a Japanese residential junction, two lanes, utility poles and wires. The hemisphere behind the lens (the 3840 px rendition, the largest Commons serves to a script): exposed to the photo's sunlit walls, its grey sky (segment.py sky matte at full width, the open sky plus the pockets seen through the canopy) swapped for the photo's graded clear sky by elevation, carried up to the zenith, by unmixing under a feathered, grown matte, so the leaves and the wires stay; the photo's own cumulus carried over the zenith on a cloud plane; then developed to the plate (develop.py): a Lab colour transfer to the photo's sunlit walls per luminance band, the road's highlights rolled off warm half a stop down, its greens desaturated and turned toward the photo's foliage, the pastel in its windows taken out, its tone-mapped crispness let down.
